mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate indicates an accommodative monetary policy stance that lowers discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days without regime dependence.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate exceeding 0.36% signals imminent monetary tightening, increasing borrowing costs and reducing corporate profitability, which drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 0.36, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in unemployment rate and declines in employment levels signal labor market deterioration, reducing consumer spending and corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises > 0.1pp and PAYEMS falls > 10k in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE rises > 0.1pp and PAYEMS falls > 10k, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts exceeding 1,100,000 units indicate robust residential construction activity, signaling strong consumer demand and economic expansion that drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when HOUST > 1100.0, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL > 235.0 and FEDFUNDS < 0.2, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
